key_insight: Re-Search turns research ideation into a Twenty Questions-style game: an LLM asks yes-or-no questions to rediscover a published paper’s core idea. This makes the model’s step-by-step exploration visible rather than judging only its final proposal.
problem_solved: Existing evaluations obscure how LLMs explore and refine research ideas, making it difficult to understand their search strategies and what limits progress.
method: Give the model only the research problem from a published paper, withholding its core idea.
Use a two-player questioning game in which the model asks yes-or-no questions to narrow down possible solutions.
Examine the questioning trajectory to study iterative idea search. The supplied abstract is truncated and does not provide complete dataset or evaluation details.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, Re-Search offers a framework for evaluating how research assistants investigate ideas, not just what they ultimately propose. It could help diagnose weaknesses in questioning and feedback-driven refinement.
visual_elements: Two-player dialogue diagram showing an LLM’s questions and yes-or-no feedback.
Branching search tree illustrating how answers narrow the space of possible research ideas.
Step-by-step pathway from a research problem to a rediscovered core idea.
Side-by-side comparison of final-output evaluation versus search-process evaluation.
paper_title: Re-Search: Dissecting LLM Ideation Through a Two-Player Questioning Game
paper_authors: Muhan Gao, Hangxiao Zhu, Xinqi Su, Yu Zhang, Daniel Khashabi
